newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight stable at 5.8 pct in cash-rich market.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight stable at 5.8 pct in cash-rich market.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate ended unchanged at 5.8 percent, keeping to the same week-long level on perceptions that the central bank did not want rates to go higher, dealers said.
"The overnight is at 5.80. There's lots of money out there," said a money market dealer.
The 5.8 percent rate is the perceived floor for the overnight set by Bank Negara.
In the broader market, interbank rates continued to be pressured on Friday as the market was still cash-rich, with some of the liquidity said to be provided by Bank Negara, dealers said.
At the morning fixing of the Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (Klibor) on Friday, the benchmark three-month rate was at 7.48 percent, its lowest for the month.
Malaysian interbank rates had moved sharply higher in mid-May in the wake of the Thai baht crisis.
Dealers said the central bank has since been trying to bring the rates down so as not to crimp economic expansion, as the higher interest rates have led banks to announce higher base lending rates.

"The move back to 'normalcy' has come sooner than expected as many had expected rates to do so in the latter part of the third quarter. This may suggest that Bank Negara was uncomfortable with the effect of the high interbank rates on the economy," said research house MMS International.
Dealers said rates were also softer after a widely expected Bank Negara lending maturity on Thursday, said to be for two billion ringgit, failed to materialise.
Such a maturity should tighten liquidity and push rates higher, they said.
One-month money was at 7.30/35 percent against 7.35/40 percent on Thursday, and three-month at 7.40/45 percent against 7.50.
One-week money was at 6.50 percent from 6.60/70.

But economists said despite its apparent easing mode this week, the central bank would not want rates to come down too much on fears of a recurrent attack on the baht and its spillover effect on the ringgit.
A big slide in interest rates would also boost spending and hike inflation which Negara wants to prevent.
The interbank rates have also been slowly trending lower to early-May levels, prior to the early attacks on the baht.
"All these suggest that there is practically no room for Klibor to edge lower, and strong support should be at 7.15/20 percent on the one-month money," said research house I.D.E.A.
